tonight.headline: Four claims, ordered. You are 2nd in priority and it resets weekly, so this queue is close to free.
body: This run covers the waiver wire only, by request. Everything on the Chem wire clears at 07:00 UTC. You are 2nd of 10, priority resets every week, and you are 0-2 with the highest points-for in the league at 235.4 — so the cost of spending priority tonight is one week of queue position, not a season.

Order the four claims below in the sequence listed. The first one you win drops you to the back for the rest of tonight's run, so the queue order is the real decision. ESPN projects you to win this week, 128.1 to 104.2.

case.label: Why the running back comes first
case.body: Jonah Coleman is the consensus number one add across Yahoo/ClutchPoints, Bleacher Report, PlayerProfiler and Roto Street Journal. Your back four is Achane, Warren, Tuten and Monangai, and the flex takes a back or a receiver, so he has a path here.

case.label: What I am not recommending
case.body: This morning's brief queued Brock Purdy ahead of everything else. I am dropping that card: you start Josh Allen every week in a one-quarterback league, so a second quarterback has no route into your lineup. The same seat spent on Coleman or Denzel Boston can actually score for you.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Denver ruling both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey fit on Thursday would cut Coleman back to a bench stash — but the claim is still right tonight, because the cost is one week of priority you get back on Tuesday.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Claims process 07:00 UTC — 01:00 Mexico City · order this FIRST
doFirst.title: Claim Jonah Coleman, drop Kyle Pitts
doFirst.subtitle: The consensus number-one add this week, and the position where your bench is thinnest.

case.label: The role
case.body: RJ Harvey sat Week 2 with a hamstring and J.K. Dobbins left with one of his own, so Coleman took over: 10 carries for 39 yards and the game-winning touchdown, plus 3 catches on 3 targets, on a running-back-high 40% of snaps. Sean Payton said all three of his backs can be a bell cow.

case.label: Why he is first in the queue
case.body: Yahoo/ClutchPoints, Bleacher Report, PlayerProfiler and Roto Street Journal all have him as the top add on the board. Bleacher Report calls him a borderline RB2 if Dobbins and Harvey both sit, with flex appeal even if they play. He faces the Rams on Sunday night.

case.label: Ignore ESPN's number here
case.body: The file projects him 1.7 points for Week 3. That is a stale projection written when Denver's backfield was healthy — Pelissero reports Dobbins is 'good' to go, but Harvey's status is unresolved and hamstrings linger. Judge this claim on the role, not the 1.7.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Pitts is 92.6% rostered and unusable here: Chem's flex is RB/WR only and Isaiah Likely holds your single tight-end slot, so Pitts's points cannot reach your lineup. That has been on the record for a week and no trade for him has cleared half a point a week.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Denver list both Dobbins and Harvey as full participants on Thursday and Friday — then Coleman is a bench stash rather than a flex option, and the claim was priority you get back next Tuesday anyway.

doFirst.sources: Yahoo Sports/ClutchPoints · Bleacher Report · FantasyPros · ESPN · Roto Street Journal

action.label: Claim Jonah Coleman · drop Kyle Pitts

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Claims process 07:00 UTC · order this SECOND
doFirst.title: Claim Denzel Boston, drop Kyle Monangai
doFirst.subtitle: The second name on every board this week, and a receiver who has produced in both games.

case.label: The role
case.body: ClutchPoints has Boston as the top receiver target of the week at 26.4% rostered: at least 50 yards and a touchdown in each of the first two weeks. Their argument is that Cleveland will play from behind all season, which gives him a safe volume floor, and they call him a WR3/flex with all-season value.

case.label: Why he fits here
case.body: Your flex is RB/WR. Boston's 164.1 season projection is above every bench player you would be dropping, and he is a rising asset (+0.28 ownership on the day) rather than a name to rent for a week.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Monangai is the fourth back on a roster that is about to add Coleman, projects 8.4 this week, and sits behind D'Andre Swift in Chicago. He was correctly protected a week ago when he was the only unchurned seat; that is no longer true.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Cleveland name a different lead receiver this week, or Boston's snap share falls once the Browns' quarterback situation settles.

action.label: Claim Denzel Boston · drop Kyle Monangai

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Claims process 07:00 UTC · order this THIRD
doFirst.title: Claim Eddy Pineiro, drop Tyler Loop
doFirst.subtitle: K2 against your K10, and an ownership anomaly: 79.5% rostered nationally and sitting free here.

case.label: The gap
case.body: ESPN ranks Pineiro the number 2 kicker this week and Loop 10th, and projects 9.4 against Loop's 8.2. That clears the one-point floor the strategy file sets for moving a kicker, which the last two weeks of Loop-versus-Pineiro comparisons did not.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: Pineiro is 79.5% rostered nationally and unclaimed in a ten-team league; Loop is 56.4%. San Francisco host Arizona.

case.label: Order it third on purpose
case.body: A kicker is worth about a point, so it goes behind two players who can score double digits. If the first two claims land you will be last in the queue and this will probably fail — that is the correct outcome, not a loss.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Pineiro appears on San Francisco's Thursday injury report, or Baltimore's implied total against Dallas rises enough to make Loop the better play.

action.label: Claim Eddy Pineiro · drop Tyler Loop

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Claims process 07:00 UTC · order this FOURTH
doFirst.title: Claim the Vikings D/ST, drop the Ravens D/ST
doFirst.subtitle: Carried from this morning's brief. Baltimore draw Dallas; Minnesota draw Tampa Bay.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN ranks Minnesota the 6th defence this week at 7.7 projected; Baltimore carries no rank at all and projects 6.0 against a Dallas offence. NBC's Week 3 column says plainly that it likes the Ravens defence but that this is not a good matchup for them.

case.label: Honest caveat on the churn rule
case.body: You added the Ravens at 07:14 on 16 September. Claims process at 07:00 today, which is fourteen minutes inside the seven-day window the strategy file closes. I am recommending it anyway because Chem priority resets weekly and defences are streamed on matchup — but it is a rule edge, not a clean case.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore finish top 12 among defences this week, or Minnesota finish outside it.

action.label: Claim Vikings D/ST · drop Ravens D/ST

whatWentWrong.title: The Purdy claim was queued ahead of the whole wire
whatWentWrong.lead: A backup quarterback cannot reach your lineup behind Josh Allen. It was first in a queue where position is the scarce thing.

case.label: The correction
case.body: This morning's brief made Brock Purdy the ELITE claim with Pitts as the drop. The same drop now buys Jonah Coleman, the consensus top add, who can actually start in your flex.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: An Allen injury, at which point a rostered quarterback matters immediately. Until then a second quarterback in a one-quarterback league scores you nothing.

whatWentWrong.title: ESPN's projection for Coleman is stale and would have hidden him
whatWentWrong.lead: 1.7 points for the back who just scored the game-winner, because the field still assumes Denver's starters are healthy.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Any ranking of this wire by weekly projection puts Coleman near the bottom. The role reporting puts him at the top. This is the case the strategy file means when it says reporting outranks projection.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Friday's designations. If Dobbins and Harvey are both full, the projection was right and the reporting was early.

worthALook.name: Xavier Worthy
worthALook.lead: The loudest ownership anomaly left on this wire, and the first name if a claim above fails.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 74.6% rostered nationally and unclaimed in a ten-team league, projected 11.5 this week with a 165.6 season number — higher than Boston's.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: He was not individually researched this run; the search budget went to the three names the boards actually moved on. Recommending a claim on ownership alone is the failure mode this log already records twice.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Coleman and Boston both fail tonight, he is the first free-agent add tomorrow once the unclaimed players clear.

worthALook.name: Adonai Mitchell
worthALook.lead: Cheap receiver depth with a real snap role, and tenth on Roto Street's board.

case.label: The case
case.body: 157.3 season projection at 17% rostered, and Roto Street Journal list him tenth among Week 3 targets.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: Boston outranks him on every board I read, and two receiver claims in one night is more churn than a 0-2 roster with the league's best points-for needs.

case.label: When to act
case.body: As a free agent tomorrow if Boston is claimed by someone above you.

doNotChase.name: Brock Purdy
doNotChase.lead: 90% rostered and free, and still the wrong claim — you start Josh Allen.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem starts one quarterback. Allen projects 23.8 this week and 347.2 for the season; Purdy cannot enter the lineup while Allen is healthy, so his effective projection to you is zero.

case.label: The cost
case.body: He would occupy the same roster seat and the same queue position as Coleman, who can start in your flex.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: An Allen injury, or a manager offering something real for a quarterback.

doNotChase.name: Tank Bigsby
doNotChase.lead: The right claim in your other league, and the wrong one here.

case.label: Why not here
case.body: Bigsby's value is as insurance for Saquon Barkley, who suffered a stinger in Week 2. Barkley is on Panda Attack's roster in Chem, not yours, so you would be renting someone else's handcuff.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Barkley being ruled out and Bigsby becoming a standalone starter in a Philadelphia offence against Chicago — then he is a free-agent add, not a priority claim.
